sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r4/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx :: 'Quality Checks' row 45 (#44) and 'Internal Quality Checks' row 45 incl. column E annotation (Mukesh: functional 60%, per-dimension own verifier weightage)
evidence: Dimension weights: tests/scoring.toml is byte-identical to the frozen template (diff empty): [weights] functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2, gates render/constraints 0.0, floor functional 0.05; this matches SKILL.md line 28 and the workbook internal annotation (functional 60%), and it is template-controlled. score.py computes sum(w*score)/sum(w) and zeroes reward unless gates pass and functional > 0.05, so functional carries 60% of the mass and gates carry none. Criterion weights (functional/judge.toml): a documented rule (comment at lines ~37-40: core legal behaviour walls/retention/holds/persistence 2.0, ordinary chat 1.5, small single behaviour 1.0, multi-part criteria take the sum) is applied consistently: wall_every_route 2.0, wall_mentions_and_links 2.0, wall_added_live 2.0, timer_changes 2.0, hold_scope_and_release 2.0, persistence 2.0, deleted_and_expired_messages 4.0 (two retention parts 2+2), signin_and_client_scope 3.0 (two confidentiality parts 1.5+1.5), sent_once_in_order 2.5 and search_and_transcript 2.5 (1.5+1.0 parts), and nested_replies, edits_and_stale_edit, safe_formatting, message_links, unread_and_new_messages_line, live_updates_keep_my_work at 1.5 each; total 33.0. This tracks the brief: instruction.md says 'Two things matter more than anything else' -- ethical walls and retention/holds. Walls + client scope = 9.0 and retention/holds/persistence = 10.0, i.e. 19/33 = 58% of functional, while ordinary chat mechanics take the rest. No style or structure criterion sits in functional. Polish (5 binary at 1.0) and visual (likert: matter_sidebar 2.0, retention_marks 2.0, transcript_page 1.0, phone_chambers 1.0) weight the brief's priority surfaces (retention marks) above generic layout; no dimension weight appears in any judge.toml [judge] block. Max non-functional contribution: polish+visual can contribute at most 0.4 of reward, always below the 0.6 functional mass; a complete functional app with zero polish/visual (0.6) outranks a perfect-looking app with minimal function. Smallest single functional criterion (1.5/33 = 0.045) does not clear the 0.05 floor, so a pretty shell passing one ordinary criterion still scores 0; the cheapest floor-clearing pretty app (one 2.0 criterion) reaches about 0.036+0.4 = 0.436. That ceiling is a consequence of the template-controlled 0.6/0.2/0.2 and 0.05 floor, which the task may not change, and every 2.0 criterion carries positive controls (e.g. persistence needs a post-restart search to find JUDGE-S1; walls require Sian's controls to work), so it is not free. Counterexamples tried: (1) broken-but-scoring app: a styled shell with no real wall enforcement loses 9/33 of functional at once and cannot earn wall credit via polish/visual, since those only grade appearance; (2) conforming alternative that could be under-credited by weights: an app that implements walls and retention correctly but has weak edits/formatting still keeps the heavy 19/33 share, so weighting favours rather than punishes the brief's core. Minor overlaps (timer label and hold mark are also observed by functional timer_changes/hold_scope_and_release and by visual retention_marks) add at most ~0.04-0.07 reward and grade different aspects (correctness vs at-a-glance visibility vs appearance); not a weight dishonesty. Limits: static review only; raw-evidence-index.json states reward discrimination/ranking runs are absent, so no measured score spread is claimed here (that evidence belongs to rows 40/42 and remains their risk).
run_verdict: PASS (static weight review; no runtime ranking measurement claimed)
